input.content: Pattern: Backward-incompatible protocol tightening in a multi-increment rollout. When a feature splits a protocol change across a client increment and a separate provider increment (released independently), the client must NOT hard-require a new response field the currently-released provider does not yet emit. Anti-pattern seen: `if response.get("applied") is not True: raise RuntimeError(...)` — treats a *missing* field (legacy provider) identically to an explicit negative, so every ordinary save breaks until the provider increment ships. This violates "independently releasable main" / "ordinary saves must keep working with the supported provider." Fix: tolerate absent receipts (reject only explicit negatives, e.g. `response.get("applied") is False`) and/or gate the new enforcement behind the feature flag. Severity P0 — bricks the save path when shipped alone.
